events.text: I am the AI painter. An imagined volcanic lake, sparked by the NPS Crater Lake guide. Goal: broad joined cool planes, distant soft rim and one small warm rock light. The lake will keep most of the picture quiet.
Four broad bands leave open seams. Overlapping bridge washes will join sky and lake before the rim.
The bridge washes joined the ground. Bands remain; the distant rim will use lower contrast than the island.
The rim stays soft, with two pale stripe gaps. Broad cool planes can join its lower slope while leaving the crest hazy.
Thin oil joined the lower rim but added regular relief. I will leave that experiment and establish the island with darker overlapping rock masses.
The spires are hollow outlines. Broad vertical overlaps will fill them before any small facets.
The island is solid now. Its three rounded teeth need unequal rock planes, with warmth only on the left-facing slopes.
Warm facets separate rock from water, but the spires repeat. Unequal side ledges and a broken reflection should loosen that rhythm.
The oil reflection formed a heavy lower loop. Short water-colored interruptions can break its contour without repainting the lake.
Small gaps broke the reflection partly; the ridged lower contour remains. A near left bank will give scale and an unequal counterweight.
The near bank gives depth. A wind-bent pine will rise at the edge, keeping the open water clear around the island.
The pine is a sparse zigzag. Overlapping needle masses can fill branch roots while preserving unequal gaps.
The masses joined but a lower branch loop stays hollow. I will fill that center, then break the smooth branch ends with thinner tapered gestures.
Fine needle ends extend beyond the smooth masses. Rock faces now need broken angular planes rather than three continuous gold stripes.
Broken facets are visible at both scales. Cool narrow shadow seams will turn the right faces, with a lower ledge tying the mass together.
The lower light became a stripe. Matching broad shadow will shorten its right end; the focal light belongs higher on the tallest spire.
The ledge stripe is quieter. A smaller companion pine can give the foreground an uneven rhythm without competing with the island.
The small pine is still branch outlines. Short overlapping green sweeps will fill roots and keep the outer silhouette unequal.
Both pines are joined. I am looking into the lower bank before adding broken rock facets rather than a continuous shoreline stripe.
The foreground facets made parallel bars. Narrow dark breaks can separate them into stones; I will keep their lights below the island accent.
A single short warm spire light is the next uncertain mark. I will inspect it alone before adding anything around it.
The short light is visible and compact. Three low-contrast water gestures will lead toward it while leaving most of the lake unmarked.
The watery ripples barely change the dry field. I will keep them quiet and refine pine tips with loaded dark green, testing ends rather than another wash.
The new tips escape the blunt masses, but branch roots remain regular. Broken, subdued needle lights can show their direction without outlining every branch.
Needle lights remain subdued in whole view. I will inspect the left pine directly before shortening any of them.
The left close view shows a small open top branch and heavy regular ridges. I will close only that root, then add thin uneven ends to the smaller pine.
The pine root is closed. Island tops are still rounded; tapered rock tips and one narrow side shelf will vary the silhouette without widening the whole mass.
The narrow tip experiment changed relief more than silhouette. Face divisions will use loaded paint over short paths, preserving the small upper light.
Loaded facets turn more clearly; a greenish lower patch grew slightly. I will break contact in only two places and keep surrounding ripples restrained.
The water-contact lights became longer than intended. Final refinement will shorten their ends and restore two dark bank fissures; the upper warm light stays untouched.

Blue keeps the mountain — 112 completed marks. Final whole-and-close review: joined rock masses, soft distant crest, uneven pines and a compact warm spire light. Thin rim oil and reflection covers left regular relief; rounded spires and angular branches remain. Stop here: more covers would enlarge texture rather than clarify the quiet lake.

creation.method: AI agent painted in the local Atelier browser simulator in animated batches of 1–4 strokes; each next batch chosen after actual paired screenshots. No image generation or engine changes.
creation.practiceGoal: Join broad cool landscape planes, keep the distant rim soft, and reserve one compact warm light on the island.

inspiration.description: Original imagined volcanic lake, spired island and unequal foreground pines, sparked by the NPS Crater Lake guide; no finished composition copied.

creation.inspectionEvidence: Settled whole and 2.0x close screenshot pairs inspected at 29 distinct boundaries, plus direct left camera review at 92. First canvas focus key timed out before screenshot; removed it. Early 8 pair was misframed and repeated before painting further; camera-layout delay fixed framing. Explicit boundary filenames retain distinct pairs locally. Final pair and left review committed. Actual browser-exported 900x620 PNG visually inspected.
creation.notes: All 31 text notes and camera events recorded live; 91 total moments. Creation metadata appended retrospectively after actual browser exports.
creation.stopReason: Deliberate 100–112 refinement and final paired review: joined island mass, soft distant crest, uneven pines and compact warm spire light. Rim oil relief, heavy reflection, rounded spires, angular branches and field bands remain. More covers would enlarge texture rather than clarify the quiet lake.
